1.name: Clean Slate
1.big: A fresh start. Twelve core screens redrawn bright and simple in the three Pokémon logo colours (red, yellow, blue), replacing the dark navy look.
1.q1: Not yet. It is tidy but flat: square cards on dotted paper, small sprites, nothing moves. Next pass needs energy and scale.
1.q2: Against the game today: light instead of dark, far bigger words, one selection colour, and every button says what it does.
1.q3: Yes. The battle screen sends Bag and Pokémon to the general pages, which hides the fight. They need their own battle pages.
1.q4: The Pause Menu is a plain list and Settings is one long tab row. Both work, neither is special yet.
1.q5: Partly. The logo colours and Poké Ball markers say Pokémon, but the shapes could be any app.

2.name: Slant & Scale
2.big: Everything leans forward. A red slash carries every title, buttons and plates are slanted, sprites are about twice as big, and the battle gets its own Bag and Switch pages.
2.q1: Better: the slash and the huge Charizard on the title grab the eye. But it is still two flat colours with no life from the Pokémon themselves.
2.q2: Pass 1 was square cards on paper. Now panels lean, the lead Pokémon gets a big card, the map is a real road with stop numbers, and Fight is the biggest button in battle.
2.q3: Done here: Bag and Switch are battle pages now, so the fight stays on screen behind them. Move details still crowd the move row and should get more room.
2.q4: The Pause Menu moved onto the red slash with the trainer standing beside it. Settings swapped the tab row for a category list on the left, which leaves room for more categories.
2.q5: More than before. Slanted bars and a road map read as modern Pokémon. What is missing is type colour, the thing every Pokémon screen is built on.
